newsitem.title: CHINA: China chemical industry '96 growth seen at 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: China chemical industry '96 growth seen at 9.7 pct.

text.p: The value of production by China's chemical industry is estimated to have grown 9.7 percent in 1996 to more than 252 billion yuan ($30.36 billion), the China Daily newspaper said on Tuesday.
Output of fertilisers last year was estimated to have hit a record 123 million tonnes, up 8.4 percent from 1995, the official newspaper said.
Pesticide production soared an estimated 23.2 percent to around 350,000 tonnes in 1996, meeting demand, it said.
Reform of the industry would continue in 1997, the newspaper quoted Chen Shineng, industry vice minister, as telling a conference last month.
Chen said more of China's chemical companies would issue shares in 1997 and companies would concentrate increasingly on profitable products and operating systems.
Priority products to be developed would include high-density fertilisers, pesticides with low toxin levels, ethylene, feed additives, paint and rubber shoes, China Daily said.
Despite steady growth in the industry, some firms continued to produce unmarketable products, it said.
The chemicals ministry would promote the creation of large enterprise groups to boost competitiveness and would promote shareholding reforms, it said.
Qualified firms would be chosen for listing on securities markets, with some being helped to issue foreign currency "B" shares in Shanghai or Shenzhen, the newspaper said without giving details.
